svg.title: DGX BasePOD versus DGX SuperPOD
svg.text: Same node, same NIC-per-GPU rule; different scale, fabric rigidity and management stack

g.title: DGX BasePOD — reference design you adapt

svg.text: DGX BasePOD — reference design you adapt
… up to ~16 nodes (verify current RA ceiling)
2–16 DGX; single leaf pair or small leaf-spine
IB Quantum-2 OR Spectrum Ethernet — customer choice
Rail-aware where possible; not a fixed SU template
Partner storage over Ethernet or IB
BCM (head node); no UFM appliance required

g.title: DGX SuperPOD — validated, replicated Scalable Units

svg.text: DGX SuperPOD — validated, replicated Scalable Units
127 nodes / 1,016 GPUs at 4 SUs; UFM appliances take one node slot
Built in SUs of 32 nodes; 1–4 SUs two-tier, core tier beyond
IB Quantum-2 NDR (classic) or Spectrum-X; rail-optimized, 1:1
Fixed cable schedule, 8 leaves per SU, spines by formula
Certified parallel storage on a dedicated fabric (> 40 GB/s per node)
BCM for nodes + UFM for the IB fabric; 4 separate networks
NVIDIA-validated component list, CVT acceptance per SU
Both: one compute NIC per GPU, BlueField-3 for storage/in-band, BMC on OOB. Exam: SuperPOD questions are SU-arithmetic questions in disguise.
